item.text: {"rubric":[{"claim_id":"c1","claim_type":"core","weight":20,"statement":"The student module defines exactly two `dspy.Predict` predictors, so `BootstrapFinetune.compile()` will iterate over two predictor slots when counting fine-tuning work.","span_ids":["module_predictors","compile_thread_check"]},{"claim_id":"c2","claim_type":"core","weight":20,"statement":"Both predictors share one LM instance, so the example specifically tests whether fine-tuning job count can be greater than model count.","span_ids":["compile_job_keys","compile_thread_check"]},{"claim_id":"c3","claim_type":"core","weight":25,"statement":"The optimizer is configured with `multitask=False`, which makes `compile()` use the predictor index in each training key and therefore create one fine-tuning job per predictor instead of merging jobs by LM.","span_ids":["compile_job_keys","compile_thread_check"]},{"claim_id":"c4","claim_type":"core","weight":20,"statement":"The program calls `compile(student, trainset=...)` with `num_threads=1`, so two distinct fine-tuning jobs exceed the available thread count and `compile()` raises `ValueError`.","span_ids":["compile_entry_and_bootstrap","compile_job_keys","compile_thread_check"]},{"claim_id":"c5","claim_type":"supporting","weight":15,"statement":"The `ValueError` is treated as the expected outcome, and the code prints or asserts message text mentioning `num_threads` and fine-tuning jobs or predictors so the job-count rule is explicit.","span_ids":["compile_thread_check"]}],"evidence":[{"span_id":"compile_entry_and_bootstrap","path":"dspy/teleprompt/bootstrap_finetune.py","start_line":60,"end_line":76},{"span_id":"compile_job_keys","path":"dspy/teleprompt/bootstrap_finetune.py","start_line":80,"end_line":101},{"span_id":"compile_thread_check","path":"dspy/teleprompt/bootstrap_finetune.py","start_line":103,"end_line":115},{"span_id":"module_predictors","path":"dspy/primitives/module.py","start_line":156,"end_line":177}]}
